question: How do UGC creators get paid?
target_query: how do ugc creators get paid
angle: Payment structures: flat fee per video, usage add-ons, raw footage, bundles, retainers, product-only deals and when to decline one; deposits; invoices; payment timing agreed in writing. No amounts.

question: How do you work out what to charge for a UGC video?
target_query: how much to charge for ugc
angle: A method, not numbers: what goes into a rate (time, deliverables, usage, revisions), base rate plus add-ons, when and how to raise it. No amounts or market claims.

question: What are usage rights in UGC?
angle: Organic vs paid use, duration, channels; why they change the price; what to put in writing. No claims about law.

question: What is whitelisting in UGC?
angle: A brand running ads from the creator's own handle; what access means; scoping duration and approvals in writing; how it differs from usage rights. Name no ad products.

question: Should you charge extra for raw footage in UGC?
angle: What raw footage is, why it lets a brand make more ads, pricing it as its own line, what to hand over. No amounts.

question: What should a UGC rate card include?
angle: Line items (base video, extra hooks, raw footage, usage, rush) and how to present them; a template table whose price column says "your price".

question: What should you agree in writing before a UGC job starts?
angle: Practical checklist: deliverables, revisions, usage, deadline, payment timing, approvals. Not legal advice; no claims about law.

question: How do you price a bundle of UGC videos?
angle: Building packages (videos, hooks, raw footage), why bundles help both sides, what changes per extra video. No amounts.

question: What is a UGC creator?
angle: Definition; difference from an influencer (the brand buys the video, not the audience); the day-to-day work.

question: Do you need followers to be a UGC creator?
target_query: do you need followers for ugc
angle: No: brands buy the video; when an audience does matter (whitelisting, posting on your account); what to build instead.

question: What should a UGC portfolio include?
angle: Sample videos across formats, hook variations, a short intro, contact; where to host it described generically; what to leave out.

question: How do you make UGC samples before any brand hires you?
angle: Products you already own; pick formats; script as if from a real brief; never imply a brand partnership that did not happen.

question: What equipment do you need to start making UGC?
angle: Phone, light, sound, a stable mount, a clean background, as categories only; what not to buy yet.

question: Should UGC creators pick a niche?
angle: Trade-offs; choosing product categories you actually use; how a niche shapes the portfolio; when to widen.

question: Can you make UGC without showing your face?
angle: Hands-only, voiceover and screen-recorded formats; follow the brief; scripting for no face.

question: What skills does a UGC creator need?
angle: Scripting, hooks, on-camera delivery, light and sound basics, editing, reading briefs, communication; how to practise each.

question: How do you write a UGC pitch email to a brand?
angle: One specific idea for their product, proof via portfolio link, a clear ask; a filled example for a described brand; what to cut.

question: How do you find brands that hire UGC creators?
angle: Signals a brand buys UGC (creator-style ads in your feed, products you use), building a list, where to pitch. Name no platforms or marketplaces.

question: What should you send a brand with a UGC pitch?
angle: Portfolio link, one relevant sample, a hook idea for their product, rates on request; what not to attach.

question: How do you follow up when a brand doesn't reply to a UGC pitch?
angle: When and how often, adding something new each time, a short example follow-up, when to stop.

question: How do you get a brand to book you again for UGC?
angle: On-time organised delivery, extra hook options, asking for feedback, proposing the next video with a concrete idea.

question: Can you pitch a brand whose product you haven't tried?
angle: Honest options: ask for a sample, say you haven't tried it, script only what you will verify; never claim use you don't have.

question: What makes a brand choose one UGC creator over another?
target_query: how to stand out as a ugc creator
angle: Craft signals the creator controls (hooks, clear audio, following a brief, turnaround). No claims about what brands report or prefer in general.

question: What goes in a UGC brief?
angle: Product, audience, key message, must-say / never-say, format, deliverables, deadline; how to read one; questions to ask. Link brief-to-script rather than repeat it.

question: What do you do when a UGC brief is vague?
angle: Questions to send back, proposing two directions, writing assumptions down before filming.

question: How should revisions work on a UGC job?
angle: Agree rounds in writing; revision vs new video; script approval before filming to avoid re-shoots.

question: What do you do when brand feedback would break the video?
angle: Word changes vs format changes; explaining in one sentence; offering an alternative that meets the note.

question: What should you deliver at the end of a UGC job?
angle: Final cuts, hook variations, raw footage if agreed, captions file, naming, a short handover note.

question: How do you name and send UGC files to a brand?
angle: Naming scheme, folders, versions, delivery-link hygiene. Name no services.

question: What do you do when a brand asks for changes after delivery?
angle: Check what was agreed; small fixes vs new work; quoting extra work politely.

question: What goes in a UGC script for a skincare brand?
angle: HAND-WRITTEN (Appendix E); ships as the pending article; never generated.

question: How do you write a UGC script for an app?
angle: The product is a screen: screen-recorded beats, phone-in-hand DO lines, one moment of value instead of a feature tour; example script.

question: How do you write a UGC script for a food or drink brand?
angle: Taste can't be filmed: reaction, sound, texture; the first bite as the turn; no health claims; example script.

question: How do you write a UGC script for a clothing brand?
angle: Fit information as the beats (size worn, how it sits, movement); try-on structure; honest sizing lines; example script.

question: How do you write a UGC script for a home or cleaning product?
angle: Show the mess and the process; a real before and after in one take; no exaggerated results; example script.

question: How do you write a fitness UGC script without promising results?
angle: No body-change promises; routine and process formats; what to say instead; example script.

question: How do you write a UGC script that doesn't sound scripted?
angle: Writing for the mouth, the read-aloud test, word-for-word lines vs talking points, a rehearsal pass; example marked line by line.

question: How do you write a call to action for a UGC ad?
angle: One ask tied to the last beat; per-goal examples (link, save, comment, shop); earned vs ad-sounding table. No ad-policy claims.

question: How is a UGC ad script different from an organic post?
angle: Same format, different viewer: name who it's for and the product sooner, explicit close; comparison table; example. No ad-policy claims.

question: How do you write a UGC script for a pet product?
angle: The pet won't follow a script: plan around real behaviour, film more than you need, owner POV; no health claims; example.

question: How many hooks should you film for one UGC video?
angle: Why brands ask for hook options; variations that change one thing; filming them in one session; table of variants; example. No testing statistics.

question: What makes a UGC hook work in an ad?
angle: The viewer doesn't know you: name the situation and the person fast, show the product's world in the first frame; examples; no algorithm claims.

question: How do you hook a UGC video when the product is in the first frame?
angle: Make the product the question, not the answer; withhold the result; a before/after pair of scripts.

question: What is a visual hook in UGC?
angle: The DO line of the first second; vague vs filmable table; motion vs still; example.

question: How do you write a negative hook a brand will approve?
angle: Aim at a habit, never the person or a competitor; brand-safe limits; table; example.

question: How do you write on-screen text for a UGC hook?
angle: Text that complements the spoken line, short enough to read while it's up (no second counts), silent viewing; example.

question: How do you write UGC hooks a brand can test against each other?
angle: Change one variable per hook (shape, opening line, first visual), keep the rest identical; table; example. No statistics.

question: How do you film UGC on a phone so it looks good?
target_query: how to film ugc on your phone
angle: Clean lens, back vs front camera, face the light, vertical framing, a stable mount, several takes. No device or app names.

question: What B-roll should you film for a UGC video?
angle: A shot list of product, hands, setting and reaction shots; filming extra for edits; tie it to the script.

question: How do you light a UGC video at home?
angle: Window light, facing the light, avoiding mixed colour, a simple lamp setup, what to avoid.

question: How do you get clear audio in a UGC video?
angle: Room choice, distance to the phone, soft furnishings, a clip-on mic as a category, checking with headphones.

question: How do you film a product demo so it looks real?
angle: One continuous take for the key moment, hands in frame, real conditions, no sped-up results.

question: Should UGC creators edit their own videos?
angle: Follow the brief; raw vs edited deliverables; a basic edit pass (cut silences, captions, pacing). No app names.

question: How should captions work in a UGC video?
angle: Burned-in vs separate, short lines that match the speech, placement clear of on-screen controls (no pixel numbers).

question: How do you film hands-only UGC?
angle: Top-down and side angles, tidy hands and background, a voiceover script, a shot list.

question: What are the main types of UGC video?
angle: One line each: testimonial, demo, unboxing, GRWM, problem-solution, before-and-after, day in the life, POV, comparison, tutorial; link live format answers. Not "most common".

question: How do you script an unboxing UGC video?
angle: The first-open moment is the hook, not the box; beats; example.

question: How do you script a get-ready-with-me UGC video?
angle: The talk track is a separate story from the routine; the product at the step where it belongs; example.

question: How do you script a testimonial-style UGC video?
angle: Real experience only; expectation → use → honest verdict with one real downside; example.

question: How do you script a problem-solution UGC video?
angle: Show the problem before the product exists in the video; the product at the turn; example.

question: How do you script a before-and-after UGC video honestly?
angle: Scripting the in-between; same light and angle; never staging an after; example.

question: How do you script a day-in-the-life UGC video?
angle: One moment for the product, not every scene; example.

question: How do you script a POV UGC video?
angle: Who the camera is; the POV label; the failure mode of a label on a non-POV video; example.

question: How do you script a UGC comparison video without naming a competitor?
angle: Compare methods or categories, state the criteria first, no rigged results; example.
